forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: The June 1 suspension of mediated talks remains fully in force. Araghchi stated June 3 that 'no formal negotiation process is underway' and 'no significant progress' had been made, with only written messages continuing. On June 10, IRGC launched strikes on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan in response to US strikes on Qeshm/Jask; on June 11 IRGC declared Hormuz 'closed to all vessels' and fired 12 ballistic missiles at Al-Azraq airbase. Qatar sent a delegation to Tehran on June 10 described only as 'bilateral discussions' — not a convened negotiating session. No Iranian MFA statement rescinding the June 1 suspension has been issued. With EOD June 16 five days away, the active military tempo and closed Hormuz declaration extinguish the near-term diplomatic path to a YES resolution.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iran's precondition of Israel halting Lebanon operations does NOT modify the resolution criteria.

indicators.name: Iranian MFA spokesman confirms re-engagement or rescinds suspension
Omani/Qatari mediator readout of a convened/held session

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed convened US-Iran negotiating session occur before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: Significant negative movement. June 10: US strikes on Iranian radar/drone sites; Iran retaliates with drone and missile strikes on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan — all intercepted. June 11: IRGC formally declares Hormuz 'closed to all vessels,' fires 12 ballistic missiles at Al-Azraq Air Base. Both sides exchanging written draft proposals through Qatar/Pakistan channels, but this explicitly falls under the ambiguity rule (written messages without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO). White House reference to a 'Witkoff-Araghchi meeting' remaining 'scheduled' predates the June 10-11 escalation; no new confirmation found. Pakistan and Qatar continue mediation contacts but no named convened session reported in the June 10-24 window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar), between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Al Jazeera/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Mere relay of written messages, or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: TIER1 report of a convened session
Iran MFA statement lifting the June 1 suspension

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: Strongly negative; p at schema floor. PortWatch recorded 2 transits on June 7 against a pre-crisis baseline of 94/day. June 10-11: IRGC formally re-declared Hormuz 'closed to all vessels,' warning any transiting vessel will be attacked. War-risk insurance at 8x pre-crisis with six P&I clubs withdrawn. CENTCOM MCM operations begun April have not produced a transit recovery trajectory approaching the 50/day threshold. Reaching 50/day avg by July 2 requires (a) an immediate ceasefire, (b) IRGC lifting the closure declaration, (c) de facto safe passage, (d) insurer reinstatement, and (e) rapid vessel mobilization — a dependency chain that cannot clear in 21 days given current military tempo.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

indicators.name: P&I war-risk cover reinstated for Hormuz transit

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: MCM operations commenced April 2026 per CENTCOM press release (USS Frank E. Peterson and USS Michael Murphy), establishing prior commencement as PARTIAL. However, the resolution window opens June 10 and requires active commencement or recommencement within this window. No new CENTCOM statement confirms active MCM operations on June 10-11. The IRGC June 10-11 'closed to all vessels' declaration and explicit hostile-fire warning make active within-window operations materially less likely absent a ceasefire. p reduced from 0.30 to 0.22 to reflect hostile-fire environment constraining MCM continuity.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10. If MCM operations were previously commenced and paused due to hostilities, recommencement within this window counts as YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Pre-window April commencement alone does not satisfy this forecast; the CENTCOM April 11 launch is context but not resolution.

indicators.name: TIER1/Pentagon report of MCM operations commencing within June 10-July 10 window
Lloyd's List clearance-lane announcement or AIS uptick toward >10 transits/day

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement on June 10-11. First reading passed June 2 (106-0); two plenum readings remain; no fixed election date inserted into bill text as of this window. Informal consensus reported around October 20 as the target date — which falls before October 27 and qualifies — but not formally inserted. Haredi parties continue to favor September over October, with intra-coalition friction capable of delaying final passage past the July 15 F6 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

indicators.name: Plenum third-reading dissolution vote held with a fixed date inserted
Haredi-parties agreement on a fixed September/Oct-20 date

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Weekly cadence holds; next review Sunday 2026-06-14. No intra-week trigger event: coalition retains operative governance capacity (dissolution bill passed 106-0 on June 2 with cross-party support, confirming functional majority); no party formally departed per resolution-criteria definition; no formal dissolution motion filed. DA extraordinary-review trigger (UTJ departure claim) rejected: 106-0 June 2 vote is inconsistent with a sub-61 coalition in crisis mode. UTJ formal-status question flagged for human verification before Sunday review.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

indicators.name: Degel HaTorah files formal dissolution motion in Knesset

forecasts.question: Will the IRGC formally lift or effectively rescind its June 10-11 'closed to all vessels' Hormuz declaration before EOD 2026-06-25?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. IRGC June 10-11 closure re-declaration amplified identically across IRNA/Tasnim/Fars — consistent with a coordinated top-level decision. Active military tempo (June 10-11 ballistic missile exchanges, US airstrikes ongoing, IRGC explicit threat to attack any transiting vessel) makes formal lift within 14 days unlikely absent a ceasefire. 22% reflects non-trivial probability of a backchannel de-escalation arrangement producing either a formal statement or de facto resumption of limited transits; the March 2 original closure was eventually partially unwound under US pressure, setting a loose base rate, but that occurred under less intense reciprocal exchange conditions.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the IRGC issues a formal statement lifting the June 10-11 closure declaration, OR if TIER1 AIS data shows >=10 commercial transits/day for two consecutive days (establishing de facto passage), before EOD 2026-06-25.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IRGC official Telegram/state media (IRNA/Tasnim) for formal lift; IMF PortWatch or equivalent AIS + one TIER1 shipping report for de facto passage threshold.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IRGC silence without a formal lift, combined with sub-10 daily transits, = NOT RESOLVED. US unilateral assertion that 'passage is safe' without IRGC statement or AIS confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IRGC formal statement lifting June 10-11 closure declaration
PortWatch/AIS records >=10 commercial transits/day for 2 consecutive days
